entries.title: Linux Detection Engineering - A Sequel on Persistence Mechanisms
entries.description: In this final part of this Linux persistence series, we'll continue exploring persistence mechanisms on Linux systems, focusing on more advanced techniques and how to detect them.

entries.title: Linux Detection Engineering - A primer on persistence mechanisms
entries.description: In this second part of the Linux Detection Engineering series, we map multiple Linux persistence mechanisms to the MITRE ATT&CK framework, explain how they work, and how to detect them.

entries.title: Beyond the wail: deconstructing the BANSHEE infostealer
entries.description: The BANSHEE malware is a macOS-based infostealer that targets system information, browser data, and cryptocurrency wallets.

entries.title: Now in beta: New Detection as Code capabilities
entries.description: Exciting news! Our Detections as Code (DaC) improvements to the detection-rules repo are now in beta. In May this year, we shared the Alpha stages of our research into Rolling your own Detections as Code with Elastic Security . Elastic is working on supporting DaC in Elastic Security. entries.title: Dismantling Smart App Control
entries.description: This article will explore Windows Smart App Control and SmartScreen as a case study for researching bypasses to reputation-based systems, then demonstrate detections to cover those weaknesses.

entries.title: BITS and Bytes: Analyzing BITSLOTH, a newly identified backdoor
entries.description: Elastic Security Labs identified a novel Windows backdoor leveraging the Background Intelligent Transfer Service (BITS) for C2. This malware was found during a recent activity group tracked as REF8747.
